title: AI × Math 每日精选
subtitle: 自动推理、形式化证明、数学智能与基础模型。
method: 公开来源采集、历史去重、规则筛选与模型审阅
method_note: 系统保存当日公开元数据，与历史日报核验后排除已报道事件；论文新版本、新修订及不同软件发布等可核实更新仍可入选，随后由指定模型阅读全文摘要并完成精选。

items.title: Math Foundation Formalization Agent: A General-Purpose Approach to Formalizing Mathematical Foundations
items.abstract_or_text: Mathematical formalization plays an important role in establishing rigorous and machine-verifiable foundations for mathematical reasoning. With the development of large language models (LLMs) and interactive theorem provers, intelligent agents offer a promising approach to automating the formalization of mathematical theories. This paper presents the Math Foundation Formalization Agent (MFF-Agent), a general-purpose intelligent agent designed to support formalization tasks across multiple mathematical domains. The agent integrates the reasoning capabilities of large language models with the formal verification capabilities of the Rocq proof assistant. It incorporates task classification, tool-assisted execution, verification feedback, and state-based task management to support the generation, refinement, and verification of formal proofs. Unlike an approach focused on a single mathematical theory, the agent is examined through case studies involving Morse--Kelley axiomatic set theory (MK), real numbers, propositional logic, and equivalences of the axiom of choice. These cases investigate its applicability across mathematical foundations and distinguish source-level completion, interactive verification, and reproducible compilation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of a unified operational framework for heterogeneous foundation-level tasks and clarify the gap between such a framework and a fully integrated mathematical foundation.
items.summary_zh: MFF-Agent 将 LLM 推理、Rocq 验证、任务分类和状态管理结合，用于跨数学基础主题的形式化工作流。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 案例覆盖集合论、实数与命题逻辑，并区分源代码完成、交互验证和可复现编译；但摘要只说明框架可行性，不足以据此宣称已实现通用自动证明。
items.abstract_zh: 数学形式化在为数学推理建立严谨且可由机器验证的基础方面发挥重要作用。随着大型语言模型（LLMs）和交互式定理证明器的发展，智能体为自动化数学理论的形式化提供了一种有前景的方法。本文提出 Math Foundation Formalization Agent（MFF-Agent），一种通用智能体，旨在支持多个数学领域的形式化任务。该智能体将大型语言模型的推理能力与 Rocq 证明助手的形式验证能力相结合。它纳入任务分类、工具辅助执行、验证反馈和基于状态的任务管理，以支持形式化证明的生成、细化和验证。不同于聚焦于单一数学理论的方法，本文通过涉及 Morse--Kelley 公理化集合论（MK）、实数、命题逻辑以及选择公理等价形式的案例研究考察该智能体。这些案例研究了其跨数学基础领域的适用性，并区分源级完成、交互式验证和可复现编译。结果表明，一个用于异构基础层任务的统一操作框架是可行的，并澄清了此类框架与完全集成的数学基础之间的差距。
items.author_line: Jiaxin Xie, Guowei Dou, Xiang Ji, Wensheng Yu

items.title: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
items.abstract_or_text: The kernel of the Lean proof assistant checks that a proof establishes its statement. Whether the statement says what was intended is left to human reviewers. This is the old problem of validating a specification, and it grows more pressing as language models write formal statements in bulk and agents edit formal developments continuously. We present ProofPatch, a tool that helps reviewers judge Lean statements and keeps their judgments valid while the development changes. A reviewer can ask the kernel targeted questions about a statement, such as whether a hypothesis is needed or whether a counterexample exists. Each decision is stored with fingerprints of the statement as Lean elaborated it and of the definitions it depends on, and any declaration can be pinned so that a patch changing it is blocked, whether a person or an agent built on a large language model (LLM) wrote the patch. Working on elaborated terms rather than source text is the central design choice: notation and formatting changes leave a decision intact, and a changed definition reaches every theorem that uses it. On 229 pairs of consecutive revisions of Mathlib, Lean's mathematics library, ProofPatch sends 118 of 12,898 synthetic decisions back for review. Every text-based alternative misses at least 38 of these or sends back at least 13 times as many. On 1,527 labeled statements, kernel evidence flags unfaithful ones with precision 0.88 to 0.96, and in 344 runs of an LLM agent no change to a pinned statement got through.
items.summary_zh: ProofPatch 以 Lean 内核证据和精化项指纹维护对形式化陈述的审阅判断，并阻止对已固定声明的改动。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 论文在 Mathlib 连续修订、标注陈述和 LLM 智能体运行中给出定量结果，针对的是“证明被内核接受但陈述偏离意图”的可审计风险。
items.abstract_zh: Lean 证明助手的内核检查一个证明是否确立其陈述。陈述是否表达了预期含义则留给人工审阅者。这是验证规格说明的老问题；随着语言模型批量编写形式化陈述、智能体持续编辑形式化开发，它愈发紧迫。我们提出 ProofPatch：该工具帮助审阅者判断 Lean 陈述，并在开发发生变化时保持其判断有效。审阅者可以就一个陈述向内核提出有针对性的问题，例如某个假设是否必要，或是否存在反例。每项决定都会连同 Lean 对陈述进行精化所得的指纹及其所依赖定义的指纹一并存储；任何声明都可以被固定，从而使更改它的补丁被阻止，无论该补丁是由人还是由基于大型语言模型（LLM）的智能体编写。以精化项而非源文本作为工作对象是核心设计选择：记法和格式的变化不会使一项决定失效，而被更改的定义会影响使用它的每个定理。在 Mathlib（Lean 的数学库）的 229 对连续修订中，ProofPatch 将 12,898 项合成决定中的 118 项送回审阅。每种基于文本的替代方法要么漏掉其中至少 38 项，要么送回的项数至少多 13 倍。在 1,527 个带标注的陈述上，内核证据以 0.88 至 0.96 的精确率标记出不忠实的陈述；在 LLM 智能体的 344 次运行中，没有任何对已固定陈述的改动得以通过。
items.author_line: Xujun Che, Depeng Xu, Jian Xiang, Taufiqua Khan

items.title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_or_text: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization has emerged as a promising approach for memory-efficient large language model (LLM) post-training, yet its reliable application to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) remains largely unexplored. Motivated by the distinct data regimes of on-policy RL and fixed-data optimization, we develop a generic variance-theoretic framework to investigate what limits the reliability of ZO gradient estimation. Our analysis reveals that estimation reliability is structurally determined by whether the two finite-difference evaluations are performed on matched data. On-policy reinforcement learning (RL) under the mismatched-data regime produces a 1/μ^2 oracle-noise amplification that sets an irreducible noise floor as the perturbation scale μ decreases, whereas Boltzmann Targeted SFT (BOLT) under the matched-data regime eliminates this amplification via noise cancellation. We further derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants that cleanly separate the two regimes. These results naturally lead to ZO-BOLT, which applies ZO optimization to BOLT's RLVR-aligned weighted-SFT objective. Controlled perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched end-to-end comparisons validate the predicted effect of data matching. Experiments across three model variants and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks further show that ZO-BOLT consistently improves over the pretrained baseline while retaining a near-inference memory footprint. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/lianmin-chen/the_cost_of_mismatch.
items.summary_zh: 该工作分析 RLVR 中零阶优化的方差来源，并以 ZO-BOLT 检验匹配数据能否避免有限差分估计的噪声放大。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 理论给出两种数据机制下带显式常数的收敛保证，并在三个模型变体、两个数学推理基准上做受控比较；结论限于所述训练设置与基准。
items.abstract_zh: 零阶（ZO）优化已成为一种有前景的方法，用于以节省内存的方式对大型语言模型（LLM）进行后训练；但其在带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）中的可靠应用仍在很大程度上未被探索。受到在线策略强化学习（RL）与固定数据优化的不同数据机制的启发，我们建立了一个通用的方差理论框架，以研究限制 ZO 梯度估计可靠性的因素。我们的分析揭示，估计可靠性在结构上由两次有限差分评估是否在匹配数据上完成所决定。在线策略强化学习（RL）在数据不匹配机制下会产生 1/μ^2 的预言机噪声放大；随着扰动尺度 μ 减小，这会形成不可消除的噪声下限。相反，处于匹配数据机制的 Boltzmann Targeted SFT（BOLT）通过噪声抵消消除了这种放大。我们还推导出带有显式常数的收敛保证，清晰地区分两种机制。这些结果自然导出 ZO-BOLT，它将 ZO 优化应用于 BOLT 与 RLVR 对齐的加权 SFT 目标。受控的扰动尺度扫描，以及匹配与不匹配的端到端比较，验证了数据匹配的预测效应。在三个模型变体和两个数学推理基准上的实验进一步显示，ZO-BOLT 相比预训练基线持续改进，同时保持接近推理阶段的内存占用。代码已公开于 https://github.com/lianmin-chen/the_cost_of_mismatch。
items.author_line: Lianmin Chen, Junbin Qiu, Chenxing Wei, Yao Shu, Kun He

items.title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs
items.abstract_or_text: Reasoning-oriented post-training enables large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks via multi-step inference. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on high-quality reasoning traces is a particularly efficient approach, but its effectiveness depends critically on careful data curation. Existing pipelines rely on a costly generate-then-filter paradigm: large pools of long reasoning traces are produced by multiple teacher models and subsequently filtered for difficulty and diversity using additional LLMs, often requiring weeks of computation. In this work, we propose SFTProbe, a fundamentally different approach that bypasses this pipeline by directly predicting the quality of reasoning data. We show that a brief LoRA-based adaptation, combined with evaluating loss on only 5% of each reasoning trace, suffices to estimate both difficulty and diversity. SFTProbe is grounded in a geometric view of post-training, where pretrained LLMs lie in a low-rank, anisotropic loss basin. By probing this basin via low-rank perturbations, we construct compact loss signatures whose clustering captures diversity, while loss at curvature inflection points provides a robust proxy for difficulty. We also provide a simple criterion for teacher selection. Empirically, our approach reduces data curation time from weeks to hours while maintaining or improving performance. Remarkably, on mathematical reasoning, 5k generated examples match the highly filtered 89k-example in OpenThoughts-Math dataset, and 7.5k generated examples outperforms it by 2.5% in accuracy. We further introduce a high-quality physics reasoning dataset, and use it to train a model that outperforms an IPhO 2025 silver-medal-winning model. The code and the dataset are released at https://bigml-cs-ucla.github.io/SFTProbe-page/.
items.summary_zh: SFTProbe 用低秩适配和短推理轨迹的损失信号预测样本难度与多样性，以缩短推理数据筛选。
items.why_it_matters_zh: 摘要报告了与 OpenThoughts-Math 过滤数据集的样本效率对照及数学推理准确率变化，并公开代码和数据；这些结果仍应按所用教师模型和评测设置解读。
items.abstract_zh: 面向推理的后训练使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过多步推断解决复杂任务。对高质量推理轨迹进行监督微调（SFT）是一种特别高效的方法，但其有效性极度依赖于细致的数据整理。现有流水线依赖昂贵的“生成后筛选”范式：由多个教师模型生成大量长推理轨迹，随后使用额外的 LLM 按难度和多样性进行筛选，这通常需要数周计算时间。在这项工作中，我们提出 SFTProbe：一种根本不同的方法，通过直接预测推理数据的质量来绕过该流水线。我们表明，短暂的基于 LoRA 的适配，加上只评估每条推理轨迹 5% 的损失，便足以估计难度和多样性。SFTProbe 建立在后训练的几何视角之上：预训练 LLM 位于低秩、各向异性的损失盆地中。通过低秩扰动探测这一盆地，我们构造紧凑的损失签名，其聚类捕捉多样性；而曲率拐点处的损失为难度提供稳健的代理指标。我们还提供了一个简单的教师选择准则。经验上，我们的方法在维持或提高性能的同时，将数据整理时间从数周缩短至数小时。值得注意的是，在数学推理上，5k 个生成样例可匹配 OpenThoughts-Math 数据集中经过高度筛选的 89k 个样例，7.5k 个生成样例则以 2.5% 的准确率优势超过它。我们还引入了一个高质量物理推理数据集，并用它训练出一个模型，该模型超过了 IPhO 2025 银牌获奖模型。代码和数据集已发布于 https://bigml-cs-ucla.github.io/SFTProbe-page/。
items.author_line: Hongyi Henry Jin, Wenhan Yang, Meysam Ghaffari, Carlos Morato, Baharan Mirzasoleiman

review.note: 按较严格证据标准仅保留 4 项：它们均有明确的形式化或数学推理任务，并报告了可检查的验证、基准或对照结果。
